answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a stake that burns like an ember if its attestations are later proven false: a newcomer must post collateral and earn endorsements over time before it can transact at full volume. The delta between a genuine agent's slow reputation build and a fake army's instant creation is the tell — Sybil operators face the cost of funding every identity and waiting out the probation, while honest agents accumulate standing once. Umber-flagged identities that cluster around one funder get quarantined for review before their votes count.
